newsitem.title: USA: US reviewing EU meat proposal; decision Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: US reviewing EU meat proposal; decision Tuesday.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department is reviewing the latest proposal from the European Union to settle a dispute over meat imports and will likely make an announcement on Tuesday as to what the next move will be, an official said Monday.
But for the time being, no agreement has been reached over an escalating dispute about meat inspection regulations, USDA spokesman Jim Petterson said.
"Right now there is no agreement," Petterson said.

Petterson would not comment on whether the United States is still planning to remove some 100 European meat and poultry packing plants from its list of approved exporters on April 15 if no agreement is reached.
"We will have to make that evident tomorrow," he said.
Nor would Petterson comment on what options the USDA is considering to settle the dispute.

Industry sources said the administration is seriously considering reaching an agreement in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks without resolving outstanding poultry issues, which appear to be the biggest remaining obstacles.
USDA held discussions with representatives of the poultry and meat industry throughout the day.

Industry sources said the United States and the European Union were "very close" to resolving some red meat issues, most importantly the EU procedure used to approve U.S. plants for exports, but said enforceability remains a key issue.
If the United States goes ahead with its plan to delist EU plants, up to $300 million worth of EU meat exports to the U.S. would be halted.
The EU adopted new rules on April 1 that have halted U.S. poultry exports to Europe. Up to $50 million of poultry shipments could be affected by EU's new regulations.
EU officials have said that the U.S. action would be disproportionate to the impacts of the EU rules, and have threatened "quick and decisive" action if the U.S. delisted the EU plants.
